description:
FILED s440 from agent D's #503 report (pre-existing). Fix shape: the `\&$x` emission site should route a resolvable-but-unbound name through p-backslash-sub (the late-binding trampoline #468/#503 already use) -- an emission change (gen bump + A/B). Bar: the repro (ref + call + $AUTOLOAD text) + `\&{"Pkg::name"}` + `\&$s` where the body is defined LATER (late binding) + `defined &$s` unchanged vs perl; a row in decl-ordering-02.t.

DONE (s446j, agent J).  `\&$s` / `\&{EXPR}` emitted (p-backslash (p-get-coderef X)) and p-get-coderef answers NIL for a name with no body -- so the ref was a SCALAR ref to nil, ref() said SCALAR where perl says CODE, and calling it reached AUTOLOAD with an EMPTY $AUTOLOAD ("main::").  Fix: one new entry point p-backslash-sub-ref, whose NAME arm is p-backslash-sub -- the same late-binding path the literal `\&NAME` spelling has always used (rule 11).  The shared front of the two questions is extracted as %p-denoted-code (function / \&foo double box / typeglob / glob ref, returning a second value so a glob with an empty CODE slot is not confused with a NAME), which p-sort-get-fn now also asks -- that is how the glob spelling `\&$globref` came to work here (it did not before).  A name whose PACKAGE does not exist has no symbol to bind late and no AUTOLOAD to reach, so it answers a lambda that dies perl's own message when CALLED -- perl returns CODE there too (probed).  MOVERS: perl-tests/ref.t 192 -> 193 and postfixderef.t 95 -> 96, both the same row `ref(\&{""})` = CODE ([perl #94476]); both baselines edited ROW BY ROW in the same commit.  Guard: Pl/t/ref-identity-01.t 39 -> 47 rows (t40-t47, four of them inverses).
subject: `\&$s` on a body-less NAME is a SCALAR ref, not a late-bound CODE ref: `ref()` = SCALAR and calling it reaches AUTOLOAD with an EMPTY name (`L::`) where perl gives CODE and $AUTOLOAD = "L::gone" (the literal `\&M::gone` spelling is right)
